insights.name: Lifestyle Longevity Risk Score
insights.desc: Composite modifiable risk index from smoking, sleep duration, exercise frequency, stress load, and alcohol patterns.
insights.range: Low risk: >70 | High risk: <40
insights.formula:
Score (0–100) = 100 − [0.25×(smoking_pack_yrs_norm) + 0.20×(alcohol_risk_norm) + 0.20×(sleep_deviation_from_7h) + 0.20×(stress_score_norm) + 0.15×(exercise_deficit_norm)]
 Higher score = lower risk. Smoking: ≥20 pack-yrs →max penalty. Sleep: <6h or >9h → graded penalty. Exercise: <150 min/wk →max penalty.

insights.name: Healthspan Trajectory Projection
insights.desc: Lifestyle-adjusted projection of remaining healthy life years, calibrated to population norms.
insights.range: Reference: chronological age − 10 yr
insights.formula:
Projected healthy years = 85 − Σ penalties
 Penalties: BMI<18.5 or >30 (−3 yr), diet_HEI<50 (−2.5 yr), activity<150 MET-min/wk (−3 yr), social_isolation (−2 yr), sleep_irregular (−1.5 yr)
 Result presented as percentile vs. age/sex-matched norms.

insights.name: HRV Aging Biomarker
insights.desc: 30-day RMSSD trend as real-time autonomic aging marker. Declining HRV correlates with accelerated biological aging.
insights.range: Optimal: >55 ms | Concern: <30 ms

insights.name: VO2 Max Biological Age Proxy
insights.desc: Cardiorespiratory fitness-based biological age estimation. VO2 max is one of the strongest predictors of longevity.
insights.range: Excellent 40s M: >46 | Poor: <35

insights.name: Sleep Architecture Score
insights.desc: Deep/REM ratio and circadian alignment score reflecting cellular repair quality and immune regulation.
insights.range: Optimal: deep >20%, REM >20%
insights.formula:
Score (0–100) = 0.35×deep_sleep_pct_norm + 0.30×REM_pct_norm + 0.25×sleep_efficiency_norm + 0.10×circadian_alignment_norm
 Optimal targets: deep sleep 15–25%, REM 20–25%, efficiency ≥85%, circadian midpoint within ±1h of population mean.

insights.name: Resting Heart Rate Trend
insights.desc: Long-term resting HR trajectory as cardiometabolic aging signal. Upward drift indicates declining fitness age.
insights.range: Optimal: 50–65 bpm | Concern: >75 bpm

insights.name: Facial Biological Age
insights.desc: Lifenome patented smartphone camera-based facial biological age estimate informed by methylation clock correlates.
insights.range: Target: ≤ chronological age
insights.formula:
Bio-age (yr) = chronological_age + Δage
 Δage = 0.35×wrinkle_depth_z + 0.30×periorbital_z + 0.25×texture_roughness_z + 0.10×symmetry_deviation_z
 All z-scores relative to same-sex, same-chronological-age cohort norms.

insights.name: Body Composition Age Index
insights.desc: Smartphone-derived body fat %, visceral fat proxy, and muscle mass index combined into a morphological age score.
insights.range: Optimal: body fat M<20%, F<28%
insights.formula:
Age offset (yr) = 0.35×body_fat_pct_z + 0.30×visceral_fat_z + 0.25×muscle_mass_z(inverted) + 0.10×WHR_z
 Final age = chronological_age + age_offset. Referenced to NHANES sex-specific percentile curves.

insights.name: Grip Strength Proxy
insights.desc: Camera-based hand posture analysis as proxy for grip strength — a validated all-cause mortality predictor.
insights.range: Optimal M: >40 kg | F: >25 kg
insights.formula:
Proxy score (0–100) = 0.60×forearm_volume_norm + 0.40×hand_posture_norm
 Calibrated against dynamometer norms (Mathiowetz 1985); sex- and age-stratified. Flags ≥20% deficit vs. norm.

insights.name: Metabolic Vitality Score
insights.desc: Fasting glucose, HbA1c, and lipid panel combined into a foundational metabolic age signal.
insights.range: Optimal glucose: 70–100 | HbA1c: <5.7%
insights.formula:
Score (0–100) = 100 − [0.25×glucose_risk + 0.20×HbA1c_risk + 0.20×LDL_risk + 0.15×HDL_benefit(inv) + 0.10×TG_risk + 0.10×TSH_deviation]
 Glucose risk: fasting ≥100 mg/dL → scaled penalty. HbA1c ≥5.7% → penalty. Each component normalized 0–25 penalty units.

insights.name: Inflammaging Index
insights.desc: Chronic low-grade inflammation composite: hs-CRP, homocysteine, ferritin as the biological age accelerator panel.
insights.range: hs-CRP optimal: <1.0 mg/L | Hcy: <10 µmol/L
insights.formula:
Score (0–100, lower=better) = 0.40×hs_CRP_norm + 0.25×homocysteine_norm + 0.20×ferritin_norm + 0.15×vitD_deficit(inv)
 hs-CRP: <1 mg/L → 0, >3 mg/L → max. Homocysteine: >10 µmol/L → graded. Vit D <30 ng/mL → penalty.

insights.name: Hormonal Vitality Score
insights.desc: IGF-1, DHEA-S, testosterone, and cortisol AM balance as validated longevity endocrine markers.
insights.range: IGF-1 optimal 40–60s: 100–200 ng/mL
insights.formula:
Score (0–100) = 0.25×IGF1_norm + 0.20×DHEA_S_norm + 0.20×testosterone_norm + 0.20×cortisol_norm(inv, optimal 10–20) + 0.15×SHBG_norm
 All normalized to sex- and age-specific reference ranges (Labcorp/Quest quintile mapping).

insights.name: ApoB / Lp(a) Cardiovascular Age
insights.desc: Most predictive lipid markers for arterial aging — ApoB and Lp(a) supersede standard LDL for longevity risk.
insights.range: ApoB optimal: <80 mg/dL | Lp(a): <75 nmol/L
insights.formula:
CVD age (yr) = chronological_age + Δ
 Δ = 0.40×ApoB_excess_yr + 0.35×Lp(a)_excess_yr + 0.15×oxLDL_z + 0.10×LDL_P_z
 ApoB: +1 yr per 5 mg/dL above 80 mg/dL. Lp(a): +1 yr per 10 nmol/L above 75 nmol/L. (Ref: ESC 2019 guidelines)

insights.name: Kidney Biological Age (eGFR)
insights.desc: eGFR and cystatin-C based kidney age — renal function declines predictably with biological aging.
insights.range: Optimal: >90 | Mild decline: 60–89
insights.formula:
Renal age (yr) = age_from_eGFR_curve + 0.20×cystatin_C_z + 0.10×creatinine_z + 0.05×BUN_z
 eGFR age: CKD-EPI equation inverted to age equivalent. eGFR 90+ → −5 yr; 60–89 → baseline; 45–59 → +8 yr; <45 → +15 yr.

insights.name: NAD+ / Mitochondrial Panel
insights.desc: NAD+, CoQ10, and glutathione as direct cellular energy and antioxidant capacity longevity biomarkers.
insights.range: Optimal NAD+: >40 µmol/L | Decline: <25

insights.name: Telomere-Associated Blood Panel
insights.desc: IL-6, TNF-α, and lymphocyte/neutrophil ratio as blood-based correlates of telomere length.
insights.range: NLR optimal: 1.0–2.5 | Concern: >3.5

insights.name: Polygenic Longevity Score
insights.desc: Lifenome 184-trait wellbeing PGS spanning fitness, nutrition, personality, and biological resilience genetics.
insights.range: Top quartile: >75th percentile
insights.formula:
Score (0–100 percentile) = weighted_PGS_average
 Component weights: APOE status (ε2=+10, ε3=0, ε4=−15 points) 0.30 + MTHFR composite 0.10 + telomere-length PGS 0.20 + 184-trait wellbeing PGS 0.40
 Final z-score converted to population percentile.

insights.name: Medical Disease PGS Panel
insights.desc: 213-condition medical PGS covering all major disease categories as all-cause mortality and morbidity modifiers.
insights.range: Elevated: >75th percentile
insights.formula:
Panel score = Σ [condition_PRS_i × disease_weight_i] / N_conditions
 Weights: circulatory 0.30 + metabolic 0.25 + cancer 0.25 + neurological 0.20
 Each PRS normalized to z-score; composite converted to 0–100 population percentile.

insights.name: Pharmacogenomics Longevity Panel
insights.desc: 193-trait PGx covering supplement absorption, drug metabolism, and statin response for longevity protocols.
insights.range: Normal / Poor / Rapid / Ultrarapid
insights.formula:
Action score (0–100) = Σ [drug_class_interaction_risk_i × prevalence_weight_i]
 CYP2D6/2C19/3A4 phenotype → 0 (normal metabolizer) to 10 (poor/ultrarapid) per enzyme. SLCO1B1 statin risk: *5 allele → +15. VDR FokI ff → +5. Mean across 193 traits, normalized.

insights.name: Circadian Rhythm Chronotype PGS
insights.desc: Genetic chronotype (morning/evening) and sleep architecture predisposition — affects biological aging rate.
insights.range: Intermediate optimal; extreme owl/lark = risk
insights.formula:
Score (0–100 alignment) = 0.35×CLOCK_gene_PGS + 0.30×PER3_VNTR_norm + 0.20×BMAL1_PGS + 0.15×chronotype_composite_PGS
 Eveningtype extreme → low score. Ref: Jones et al. 2019 genome-wide study (napping, sleep timing, 351 loci).

insights.name: Full Genome Longevity Scan
insights.desc: WGS improves PRS accuracy by 25–35% and discovers ultra-rare structural variants missed by arrays and exome.
insights.range: WGS PRS ±1.5 SD from mean

insights.name: Microbiome Diversity Longevity Index
insights.desc: Alpha and beta diversity as independent aging predictors — centenarians show distinct microbiome signatures.
insights.range: Optimal H: >3.0 | Concern: <2.0
insights.formula:
Score (0–100) = 0.35×Shannon_H_norm + 0.25×Akkermansia_pct_norm + 0.20×Bifidobacterium_pct_norm + 0.20×FB_ratio_norm(inv)
 Shannon H: <2.5→low, >3.5→high. F:B ratio: >3:1→penalty. Akkermansia <1%→penalty. Calibrated to Lifenome population median.

insights.name: Leaky Gut & Systemic Inflammation
insights.desc: Intestinal permeability markers measured via microbiome composition correlates affecting inflammaging.
insights.range: Optimal: <3 | High risk: >7
insights.formula:
Risk score (0–100, lower=better) = 0.40×LPS_bacteria_pct_norm + 0.35×barrier_species_deficit + 0.25×zonulin_correlate_norm
 LPS producers: Proteobacteria >10%→high risk. Mucosal barrier taxa (F. prausnitzii, Akkermansia) deficit → graded penalty.

insights.name: Functional Longevity Metabolomics
insights.desc: Butyrate producers, SCFA synthesis capacity, and tryptophan metabolism from shotgun functional analysis.
insights.range: Butyrate genes: optimal >1.5 RPKM
insights.formula:
Score (0–100) = 0.30×butyrate_gene_density + 0.25×SCFA_producer_pct + 0.25×tryptophan_pathway_capacity + 0.20×serotonin_pathway_score
 All normalized to gut metagenome depth. Butyrate pathway (but, buk genes) RPKM >1000 → optimal.

insights.name: Epigenetic Biological Age (DNAmAge)
insights.desc: Horvath, GrimAge, DunedinPACE, and PhenoAge clocks — gold-standard multi-algorithm biological age battery.
insights.range: Target: ≤ chronological age
insights.formula:
Bio-age (yr) = weighted_average([Horvath×0.25, GrimAge×0.35, DunedinPACE_est×0.25, PhenoAge×0.15])
 DunedinPACE expressed as 'yr of bio-aging per yr': >1.0 → accelerated. Result displayed as age estimate + acceleration (yr above/below chronological).

insights.name: Epigenetic Age Acceleration
insights.desc: Age gap vs. chronological age — the most actionable longevity intervention target available.
insights.range: Optimal: ≤0 yr | High: >5 yr acceleration
insights.formula:
Acceleration (yr) = 0.40×AgeAccelGrim + 0.35×DunedinPACE_deviation + 0.25×AgeAccelHorvath
 Positive = faster aging. Clinical threshold: >3 yr acceleration = elevated risk. Ref: Lu et al. (GrimAge), Belsky et al. (DunedinPACE).

insights.name: Methylation-Based Disease Risk Scores
insights.desc: DNAm-derived risk scores for cardiovascular disease, T2DM, and cancer independent of genetic risk.
insights.range: Elevated: >75th percentile
insights.formula:
Composite risk (0–100) = 0.35×DNAm_CVD_score_norm + 0.30×DNAm_T2DM_norm + 0.20×cancer_CpG_risk_norm + 0.15×immune_age_norm
 Each methylation score derived from validated CpG panels (Mendelian randomization-confirmed loci).

insights.name: Heavy Metal & Toxin Burden Index
insights.desc: Function Health includes mercury and lead in standard membership. Chronic heavy metal accumulation accelerates aging, impairs cognition, and drives cardiovascular and kidney disease. Lead, mercury, arsenic, and cadmium panel.
insights.range: Mercury: <5 μg/L | Lead: <3.5 μg/dL | Arsenic: <20 μg/L
insights.formula:
Burden score (0–100, lower=better) = 0.25×Pb_norm + 0.25×Hg_norm + 0.20×As_norm + 0.15×Cd_norm + 0.10×Al_norm + 0.05×Tl_norm
 Reference: CDC NHANES 95th-pct upper limits. Pb >5 µg/dL → high. Hg >5 µg/L → high. Any element >99th pct → critical flag.

insights.name: Autoimmune Surveillance Index
insights.desc: Function Health data shows 23% of members have elevated autoimmune antibodies — most entirely asymptomatic. ANA screen, anti-dsDNA, TPO, TgAb, and anti-CCP provide early autoimmune detection before clinical symptoms emerge.
insights.range: ANA negative | TPO Ab: <35 IU/mL | Anti-dsDNA: <30 IU/mL
insights.formula:
Risk score (0–100) = 0.20×ANA_titer_norm + 0.15×anti_dsDNA_norm + 0.15×TPO_Ab_norm + 0.15×TgAb_norm + 0.10×anti_CCP_norm + 0.10×RF_norm + 0.15×complement_deficit(inv)
 ANA ≥1:160 → elevated. Pattern (speckled/homogenous) modifies score. C3/C4 <reference → +10 points.

insights.name: Blood-Based Biological Age
insights.desc: Biological age calculated from 18 key blood biomarkers using ML algorithms trained on 42,000+ samples (methodology: InsideTracker InnerAge 2.0 + PhenoAge). Biomarkers weighted by their correlation with chronological aging: glucose, LDL, albumin, hematocrit, lymphocytes, GGT, HbA1c, triglycerides, cortisol, DHEA-S, ferritin, vitamin D, hs-CRP, insulin, MCHC, creatinine, uric acid, WBC.
insights.range: Optimal: ≥3 years younger than chronological | Concern: >3 years older
insights.formula: Bio-age = PhenoAge 9-biomarker algorithm. (Precision Medicine context)

insights.name: Epigenetic Biological Age (Methylation)
insights.desc: DNA methylation-based biological age using 4 validated epigenetic clocks: Horvath clock (pan-tissue), GrimAge (strongest all-cause mortality predictor), PhenoAge (phenotypic health proxy), and DunedinPACE (real-time aging speed). GrimAge acceleration >3 years is a major actionable threshold. Covers 850,000 CpG sites.
insights.range: Ideal: clock age ≤ chronological | Alert: GrimAge >3 yr acceleration
insights.formula: Bio-age = 0.30×Horvath + 0.30×GrimAge + 0.20×DunedinPACE + 0.10×PhenoAge + 0.10×other clocks. (Precision Medicine context)

insights.name: Actuarial Age (Lifestyle & Demographic)
insights.desc: Validated actuarial biological age calculation from lifestyle and demographic inputs, based on RealAge and Levine mortality risk models. Factors: smoking history, alcohol intake, BMI, physical activity level, diet quality score, sleep duration, psychosocial stress, social connectedness, education, income proxy, environmental exposures, and medical history. Each factor is weighted by its effect size on all-cause mortality.
insights.range: Optimal: ≥5 years younger | Danger zone: >5 years older
insights.formula: Actuarial age = chronological + lifestyle penalties. (Precision Medicine context)

insights.name: Physiological Age (HRV · VO₂Max · HR · BP)
insights.desc: Composite physiological age score derived from four objective performance biomarkers: resting heart rate variability (RMSSD — validated vs. chronological age normative curves), VO₂max (cardiorespiratory fitness age from submaximal exercise), resting heart rate trend, and blood pressure index. Each metric is z-scored against age/sex-matched population norms and combined into a single physiological age.
insights.range: Optimal: ≥5 years younger | HRV age: RMSSD age-matched percentile >60th
insights.formula: Physiological age = 0.30×HRV + 0.30×VO2max + 0.25×RHR + 0.15×BP. (Precision Medicine context)

insights.name: Cardiovascular System Age
insights.desc: Dedicated biological age for the cardiovascular system integrating vascular stiffness proxies, lipid particle quality, inflammatory burden, and hemodynamic markers. Based on the Framingham Heart Age model extended with ApoB, Lp(a), NT-proBNP, and hs-CRP weighting. Expresses how much older or younger your cardiovascular system is than your chronological age.
insights.range: Optimal: ≥5 yr younger | Alert: >5 yr older | Critical: >10 yr older
insights.formula: CV age = composite of 9 CV biomarkers age-converted. (Precision Medicine context)

insights.name: Metabolic System Age
insights.desc: Biological age of the metabolic system derived from glucose regulation, insulin sensitivity, lipid metabolism, liver function, and body composition markers. The MetaboAge algorithm weights HOMA-IR, HbA1c, fasting insulin, triglycerides, ALT, GGT, uric acid, and adipokines against age-matched population norms.
insights.range: Optimal: ≥3 yr younger | Metabolic syndrome threshold: >8 yr older
insights.formula: Metabolic age = composite of 7 metabolic biomarkers. (Precision Medicine context)

insights.name: Immune System Age (Immunological Age)
insights.desc: Immunological age derived from the composition of white blood cell subpopulations, inflammatory cytokines, and autoimmune markers. Based on the iAge (inflammatory age) framework from Stanford and the immunosenescence scoring of Lehallier et al. (2019). Captures both inflammaging (chronic low-grade inflammation) and immunosenescence (loss of adaptive immune capacity).
insights.range: iAge optimal: <30 | Alert: >chronological | Immunosenescence: NLR >3.0
insights.formula: iAge = 0.25×NLR + 0.20×CXCL9 + 0.15×hs-CRP + 0.15×IL-6 + 0.25×other. (Precision Medicine context)

insights.name: Respiratory System Age
insights.desc: Biological age of respiratory function integrating blood-based markers of pulmonary capacity and oxygenation with wearable SpO₂ and resting respiratory rate. Proxy for FEV1/FVC ratio decline using SERPINA1, CRP, and RBC indices. Validated against NHANES spirometry normative age curves.
insights.range: Optimal: ≥3 yr younger | SpO₂ <95% resting = significant aging signal
insights.formula: Resp age = composite of 6 respiratory biomarkers. (Precision Medicine context)

insights.name: Musculoskeletal System Age
insights.desc: Biological age of the musculoskeletal system derived from bone turnover markers, inflammatory burden on joints, muscle catabolism indicators, and hormonal support for lean mass. Integrates vitamin D, testosterone/DHEA-S, IGF-1, and bone resorption/formation markers into a composite MSK age score.
insights.range: Optimal: ≥3 yr younger | Osteoporosis risk: CTX-I high + low osteocalcin
insights.formula: MSK age = composite of 8 musculoskeletal biomarkers. (Precision Medicine context)

insights.name: Neuroinflammation Index
insights.desc: Composite of hs-CRP, IL-6, TNF-α, and homocysteine to quantify systemic and central nervous system inflammatory burden linked to depression, cognitive decline, and anxiety disorders.
insights.range: Optimal: <25 | Elevated: 25–60 | High burden: >60
insights.formula:
Score (0–100, lower=better) = 0.30×hs_CRP_norm + 0.25×IL6_norm + 0.20×TNF_alpha_norm + 0.15×homocysteine_norm + 0.10×NLR_norm
 hs-CRP >3 mg/L → chronic low-grade neuroinflammation. Homocysteine >15 → neurotoxic risk. IL-6 primary mediator.

insights.name: Cortisol Stress Burden Score
insights.desc: Morning cortisol and DHEA-S ratio reflecting HPA-axis dysregulation, burnout risk, and chronic stress load. Chronically elevated cortisol is causal in anxiety, depression, memory impairment, and sleep disruption.
insights.range: Healthy ratio: 5–10 | Burnout risk: >15 | Adrenal fatigue: <3
insights.formula:
Score (0–100, lower=better) = 0.45×cortisol_AM_norm + 0.35×cortisol_DHEA_ratio_norm + 0.20×DHEA_S_inv
 Cortisol/DHEA-S >10:1 → HPA dysregulation. Cortisol >22 µg/dL → hypercortisolism flag.

insights.name: Serotonin Precursor Availability
insights.desc: Tryptophan and its ratio to competing large neutral amino acids (LNAAs) determines CNS serotonin synthesis capacity. Low ratio is a validated biological marker for depression vulnerability and carbohydrate craving.
insights.range: Optimal: >0.12 | Depleted: <0.08
insights.formula:
Score (0–100) = 0.45×tryptophan_norm + 0.20×Trp_LNAA_ratio_norm + 0.15×tyrosine_norm + 0.10×phenylalanine_norm + 0.10×BCAA_ratio_inv
 Trp:LNAA ratio > 0.1 → adequate brain serotonin synthesis. Low Trp → depression/anxiety vulnerability.

insights.name: Dopamine & Catecholamine Balance
insights.desc: Tyrosine availability (dopamine precursor), phenylalanine, and plasma catecholamine proxies reflecting reward circuitry, motivation, focus, and ADHD-related pathways.
insights.range: Optimal: >1.5 | Depleted: <1.0
insights.formula:
Score (0–100) = 0.45×tyrosine_norm + 0.30×Tyr_Phe_ratio_norm + 0.25×HVA_norm
 Tyrosine:phenylalanine >1.2:1 → adequate catecholamine synthesis. HVA (dopamine metabolite): <2 nmol/mL → low dopamine turnover.

insights.name: Mood-Nutrient Deficiency Panel
insights.desc: Critical neuronutrients whose deficiency is causally linked to depression, anxiety, fatigue, and cognitive impairment. Inspired by Function Health's finding that 38% of users are deficient in ≥1 key brain nutrient.
insights.range: Vit D optimal: 40–80 ng/mL | B12: >400 pg/mL | Omega-3: >8%

insights.name: Thyroid-Mood Connection Score
insights.desc: Subclinical hypothyroidism and thyroid autoimmunity are strongly associated with depression, brain fog, fatigue, and anxiety. Full thyroid panel including TPO antibodies (elevated in ~23% of population per Function Health data).
insights.range: TSH optimal: 1.0–2.5 mIU/L | TPO Ab: <35 IU/mL
insights.formula:
Score (0–100) = 0.25×TSH_norm + 0.25×fT3_norm + 0.20×fT4_norm + 0.15×TPO_Ab_inv + 0.15×TgAb_inv
 Subclinical hypothyroidism (TSH 4–10): −20 pts. Elevated TPO Ab → Hashimoto → mood vulnerability. rT3 elevation → cellular hypothyroid.

insights.name: Brain Aging & Alzheimer's Risk Score
insights.desc: Blood-based neurodegenerative biomarker panel including p-tau217 (AUC 0.93–0.96 for Alzheimer's per Nature Medicine 2025), GFAP, and NfL. Function Health reports 14% of members have elevated p-tau217. Integrated with APOE genotype from DNA.
insights.range: p-tau217 low risk: <0.4 pg/mL | High risk: >1.0 pg/mL
insights.formula:
Score (0–100, lower=better) = 0.30×p_tau217_norm + 0.25×GFAP_norm + 0.25×NfL_norm + 0.20×Ab42_40_ratio_inv
 Aβ42/40 <0.09 → amyloid pathology signal. p-tau217 → primary AT(N) AD biomarker (Ref: Hansson et al. 2023). GFAP → astrocytic injury.

insights.name: HPA-Axis Resilience Index
insights.desc: Combined cortisol, ACTH, and adrenal reserve markers reflecting hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal function. Predicts stress resilience, post-traumatic recovery capacity, and treatment response in anxiety and depression.
insights.range: Resilient: >65 | Vulnerable: 35–65 | Depleted: <35
insights.formula:
Score (0–100) = 0.30×cortisol_AM_norm + 0.25×ACTH_norm + 0.20×DHEA_S_norm + 0.15×aldosterone_norm + 0.10×CAR_norm
 CAR (cortisol awakening response) optimal: 50–100% increase above baseline at 30 min. Blunted CAR → PTSD/burnout marker.

insights.name: Gut-Brain Axis Health Score
insights.desc: Validated blood proxies of gut microbiome health (InsideTracker methodology: hsCRP, cortisol, HDL, triglycerides, glucose, HbA1c) plus LPS and zonulin markers of intestinal permeability linked to mood disorders via vagus nerve signaling.
insights.range: Optimal: >70 | Dysbiosis risk: <45
insights.formula:
Score (0–100) = 0.20×hs_CRP_inv + 0.15×cortisol_inv + 0.15×HDL_norm + 0.15×TG_inv + 0.15×glucose_inv + 0.10×HbA1c_inv + 0.10×LPS_inv
 Gut permeability → systemic LPS → neuroinflammation cascade. Score integrates metabolic and inflammatory gut-brain mediators.

insights.name: Metabolic-Psychiatric Risk Index
insights.desc: Insulin resistance, blood sugar dysregulation, and lipid imbalance are bidirectionally linked to depression, anxiety, and cognitive decline. Adapted from InsideTracker's metabolism + cognition cross-category scoring.
insights.range: HOMA-IR optimal: <1.5 | Insulin resistance: >2.5

 Insulin resistance → 50% increased depression risk (Ref: Pearson et al. 2021). Metabolic syndrome → 40% increased anxiety.

insights.name: Oxidative Stress & Antioxidant Capacity
insights.desc: Excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) damage neuronal membranes and mitochondria, driving neuroinflammation, depression, and cognitive aging. Panel includes 8-OHdG, glutathione, and uric acid.

 8-OHdG >15 ng/mg creatinine → high DNA oxidative damage. GSH: target >700 µmol/L. Uric acid: mild antioxidant at normal levels.

insights.name: Sex Hormone-Mental Health Bridge
insights.desc: Testosterone, estradiol, and progesterone fluctuations modulate serotonin, GABA, and dopamine systems. Critical for premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), postpartum depression, perimenopause mood, and male testosterone-related depression.
insights.range: E2 optimal (women): 30–200 pg/mL | Testosterone (men): 400–700 ng/dL
insights.formula:

 Low testosterone (m: <300 ng/dL) → depression. Low E2 (f) → cognitive decline, mood disruption. SHBG high → bioavailable T low.

insights.name: Sleep Quality Biomarker Score
insights.desc: Blood markers correlated with deep sleep, REM quality, and sleep architecture. Inspired by InsideTracker's sleep healthspan category. Melatonin pathway markers, magnesium, and circadian cortisol profiling.

 Mg <1.8 mg/dL → GABA and melatonin synthesis impaired. Vit D <30 → circadian rhythm disruption.

insights.name: Polygenic Depression & Anxiety Risk
insights.desc: Multi-locus genetic risk score aggregating 100+ validated SNPs across serotonin transporter (5-HTTLPR), BDNF Val66Met, COMT Val158Met, FKBP5, CRHR1, and other stress-response and neurotransmitter genes.

 5-HTTLPR S/S → 2× depression risk under stress. FKBP5 rs1360780 T allele → PTSD vulnerability.

insights.name: Neurotransmitter Metabolism Genotype

 COMT Met/Met → slow dopamine degradation (worrier). Met/Val → intermediate. Val/Val → fast (warrior).

insights.name: APOE & Neurodegeneration Risk Score

 APOE ε4 doubles lifetime AD risk per allele. TOMM40 poly-T length modulates age of onset.

 NR3C1 BclI C allele → GR hypersensitivity → PTSD vulnerability. NPY rs16139 CC → resilience advantage.

 PHQ-9 ≥10 → moderate depression. GAD-7 ≥10 → moderate anxiety. PSQI >5 → poor sleep quality.

 Social jetlag >2h → 1.4× metabolic syndrome risk. Evening chronotype with early schedule → highest disruption.

insights.name: HRV-Based Stress & Recovery Index

 RMSSD <20 ms → sympathetic dominance/high stress. >50 ms → parasympathetic tone. HRV decline >15% over 7 days → recovery alert.

insights.name: Sleep Architecture & Restorative Sleep Score
insights.desc: Deep sleep (N3) percentage, REM latency, sleep efficiency, and nocturnal HRV from wearable device correlated with cognitive performance, emotional regulation, and mood stability next-day.

Score (0–100) = 0.30×deep_sleep_norm(target 15–25%) + 0.25×REM_norm(target 20–25%) + 0.20×efficiency_norm + 0.15×latency_inv(target <20 min) + 0.10×nocturnal_HRV_norm
 Deep sleep <10% → GH and memory consolidation deficit. REM <15% → emotional processing impaired.

insights.name: Brain Epigenetic Age (DNAmAge)
insights.desc: DNA methylation-based biological age clocks (Horvath, GrimAge, PhenoAge) applied to brain-relevant CpG sites. GrimAge is the strongest predictor of mortality and cognitive aging; acceleration >3 years indicates elevated risk.

 GrimAge acceleration >3 yr → significantly elevated dementia risk. DunedinPACE >1.0 → faster cognitive aging.

 FKBP5 intron7 hypomethylation → trauma-related PTSD (Ref: Klengel et al. 2013 Nat Neurosci).

 L. rhamnosus JB-1 → GABA-A receptor upregulation → anxiolytic effect. Kynurenine:tryptophan ratio >40 → neuroinflammatory pattern.

insights.name: Nutritional Gap Score
insights.desc: Composite index of micronutrient deficiency risk across 12 key vitamins and minerals based on dietary intake patterns, blood biomarkers, and genetic metabolism variants.
insights.range: Optimal: >75 | At-risk: <50
insights.formula:
Score (0–100, lower=better) = Σ [deficiency_i × weight_i]
 Vit D 0.15 + B12 0.12 + ferritin 0.12 + zinc 0.10 + Mg 0.10 + omega-3 0.10 + folate 0.10 + iodine 0.08 + selenium 0.08 + CoQ10 0.05 + K2 0.05 + choline 0.05
 Deficiency = (optimal_level − actual) / optimal_range.

insights.name: Metabolic Flexibility Index
insights.desc: Measures the body's ability to switch between carbohydrate and fat fuel sources based on fasting insulin, triglycerides, glucose variability, and ketone capacity.

insights.formula:
Score (0–100) = 0.30×HOMA_IR_inv + 0.25×fasting_insulin_inv + 0.20×TG_inv + 0.15×BHB_norm(target 0.1–0.5 mmol/L in fed state) + 0.10×FFA_norm
 HOMA-IR <1.0 → high flexibility. BHB elevation → ketone utilization capacity. TG:HDL <1.5 → insulin sensitive.
